vulg: Iacobus Dei et Domini nostri Iesu Christi servus duodecim tribubus quae sunt in dispersione salutem
clem: Jacobus, Dei et Domini nostri Jesu Christi servus, duodecim tribubus, qu sunt in dispersione, salutem.
tr: ιακωβος θεου και κυριου ιησου χριστου δουλος ταις δωδεκα φυλαις ταις εν τη διασπορα χαιρειν
kjv: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.

vulg: omne gaudium existimate fratres mei cum in temptationibus variis incideritis
clem: Omne gaudium existimate fratres mei, cum in tentationes varias incideritis:
tr: πασαν χαραν ηγησασθε αδελφοι μου οταν πειρασμοις περιπεσητε ποικιλοις
kjv: My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations;

vulg: scientes quod probatio fidei vestrae patientiam operatur
clem: scientes quod probatio fidei vestr patientiam operatur.
tr: γινωσκοντες οτι το δοκιμιον υμων της πιστεως κατεργαζεται υπομονην
kjv: Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience.

vulg: patientia autem opus perfectum habeat ut sitis perfecti et integri in nullo deficientes
clem: Patientia autem opus perfectum habet: ut sitis perfecti et integri in nullo deficientes.
tr: η δε υπομονη εργον τελειον εχετω ινα ητε τελειοι και ολοκληροι εν μηδενι λειπομενοι
kjv: But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.

vulg: si quis autem vestrum indiget sapientiam postulet a Deo qui dat omnibus affluenter et non inproperat et dabitur ei
clem: Si quis autem vestrum indiget sapientia, postulet a Deo, qui dat omnibus affluenter, et non improperat: et dabitur ei.
tr: ει δε τις υμων λειπεται σοφιας αιτειτω παρα του διδοντος θεου πασιν απλως και μη ονειδιζοντος και δοθησεται αυτω
kjv: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

vulg: postulet autem in fide nihil haesitans qui enim haesitat similis est fluctui maris qui a vento movetur et circumfertur
clem: Postulet autem in fide nihil hsitans: qui enim hsitat, similis est fluctui maris, qui a vento movetur et circumfertur:
tr: αιτειτω δε εν πιστει μηδεν διακρινομενος ο γαρ διακρινομενος εοικεν κλυδωνι θαλασσης ανεμιζομενω και ριπιζομενω
kjv: But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.

vulg: non ergo aestimet homo ille quod accipiat aliquid a Domino
clem: non ergo stimet homo ille quod accipiat aliquid a Domino.
tr: μη γαρ οιεσθω ο ανθρωπος εκεινος οτι ληψεται τι παρα του κυριου
kjv: For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.

vulg: vir duplex animo inconstans in omnibus viis suis
clem: Vir duplex animo inconstans est in omnibus viis suis.
tr: ανηρ διψυχος ακαταστατος εν πασαις ταις οδοις αυτου
kjv: A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.

vulg: glorietur autem frater humilis in exaltatione sua
clem: Glorietur autem frater humilis in exaltatione sua:
tr: καυχασθω δε ο αδελφος ο ταπεινος εν τω υψει αυτου
kjv: Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted:

vulg: dives autem in humilitate sua quoniam sicut flos faeni transibit
clem: dives autem in humilitate sua, quoniam sicut flos fni transibit;
tr: ο δε πλουσιος εν τη ταπεινωσει αυτου οτι ως ανθος χορτου παρελευσεται
kjv: But the rich, in that he is made low: because as the flower of the grass he shall pass away.

vulg: exortus est enim sol cum ardore et arefecit faenum et flos eius decidit et decor vultus eius deperiit ita et dives in itineribus suis marcescet
clem: exortus est enim sol cum ardore, et arefecit fnum, et flos ejus decidit, et decor vultus ejus deperiit: ita et dives in itineribus suis marcescet.
tr: ανετειλεν γαρ ο ηλιος συν τω καυσωνι και εξηρανεν τον χορτον και το ανθος αυτου εξεπεσεν και η ευπρεπεια του προσωπου αυτου απωλετο ουτως και ο πλουσιος εν ταις πορειαις αυτου μαρανθησεται
kjv: For the sun is no sooner risen with a burning heat, but it withereth the grass, and the flower thereof falleth, and the grace of the fashion of it perisheth: so also shall the rich man fade away in his ways.

vulg: beatus vir qui suffert temptationem quia cum probatus fuerit accipiet coronam vitae quam repromisit Deus diligentibus se
clem: Beatus vir qui suffert tentationem: quoniam cum probatus fuerit, accipiet coronam vit, quam repromisit Deus diligentibus se.
tr: μακαριος ανηρ ος υπομενει πειρασμον οτι δοκιμος γενομενος ληψεται τον στεφανον της ζωης ον επηγγειλατο ο κυριος τοις αγαπωσιν αυτον
kjv: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.

vulg: nemo cum temptatur dicat quoniam a Deo temptor Deus enim intemptator malorum est ipse autem neminem temptat
clem: Nemo cum tentatur, dicat quoniam a Deo tentatur: Deus enim intentator malorum est: ipse autem neminem tentat.
tr: μηδεις πειραζομενος λεγετω οτι απο του θεου πειραζομαι ο γαρ θεος απειραστος εστιν κακων πειραζει δε αυτος ουδενα
kjv: Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man:

vulg: unusquisque vero temptatur a concupiscentia sua abstractus et inlectus
clem: Unusquisque vero tentatur a concupiscentia sua abstractus, et illectus.
tr: εκαστος δε πειραζεται υπο της ιδιας επιθυμιας εξελκομενος και δελεαζομενος
kjv: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.

vulg: dein concupiscentia cum conceperit parit peccatum peccatum vero cum consummatum fuerit generat mortem
clem: Deinde concupiscentia cum conceperit, parit peccatum: peccatum vero cum consummatum fuerit, generat mortem.
tr: ειτα η επιθυμια συλλαβουσα τικτει αμαρτιαν η δε αμαρτια αποτελεσθεισα αποκυει θανατον
kjv: Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.

vulg: nolite itaque errare fratres mei dilectissimi
clem: Nolite itaque errare, fratres mei dilectissimi.
tr: μη πλανασθε αδελφοι μου αγαπητοι
kjv: Do not err, my beloved brethren.

vulg: omne datum optimum et omne donum perfectum desursum est descendens a Patre luminum apud quem non est transmutatio nec vicissitudinis obumbratio
clem: Omne datum optimum, et omne donum perfectum desursum est, descendens a Patre luminum, apud quem non est transmutatio, nec vicissitudinis obumbratio.
tr: πασα δοσις αγαθη και παν δωρημα τελειον ανωθεν εστιν καταβαινον απο του πατρος των φωτων παρ ω ουκ ενι παραλλαγη η τροπης αποσκιασμα
kjv: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.

vulg: voluntarie genuit nos verbo veritatis ut simus initium aliquod creaturae eius
clem: Voluntarie enim genuit nos verbo veritatis, ut simus initium aliquod creatur ejus.
tr: βουληθεις απεκυησεν ημας λογω αληθειας εις το ειναι ημας απαρχην τινα των αυτου κτισματων
kjv: Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.

vulg: scitis fratres mei dilecti sit autem omnis homo velox ad audiendum tardus autem ad loquendum et tardus ad iram
clem: Scitis, fratres mei dilectissimi. Sit autem omnis homo velox ad audiendum: tardus autem ad loquendum, et tardus ad iram.
tr: ωστε αδελφοι μου αγαπητοι εστω πας ανθρωπος ταχυς εις το ακουσαι βραδυς εις το λαλησαι βραδυς εις οργην
kjv: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:

vulg: ira enim viri iustitiam Dei non operatur
clem: Ira enim viri justitiam Dei non operatur.
tr: οργη γαρ ανδρος δικαιοσυνην θεου ου κατεργαζεται
kjv: For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.

vulg: propter quod abicientes omnem inmunditiam et abundantiam malitiae in mansuetudine suscipite insitum verbum quod potest salvare animas vestras
clem: Propter quod abjicientes omnem immunditiam, et abundantiam maliti, in mansuetudine suscipite insitum verbum, quod potest salvare animas vestras.
tr: διο αποθεμενοι πασαν ρυπαριαν και περισσειαν κακιας εν πραυτητι δεξασθε τον εμφυτον λογον τον δυναμενον σωσαι τας ψυχας υμων
kjv: Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.

vulg: estote autem factores verbi et non auditores tantum fallentes vosmet ipsos
clem: Estote autem factores verbi, et non auditores tantum: fallentes vosmetipsos.
tr: γινεσθε δε ποιηται λογου και μη μονον ακροαται παραλογιζομενοι εαυτους
kjv: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.

vulg: quia si quis auditor est verbi et non factor hic conparabitur viro consideranti vultum nativitatis suae in speculo
clem: Quia si quis auditor est verbi, et non factor, hic comparabitur viro consideranti vultum nativitatis su in speculo:
tr: οτι ει τις ακροατης λογου εστιν και ου ποιητης ουτος εοικεν ανδρι κατανοουντι το προσωπον της γενεσεως αυτου εν εσοπτρω
kjv: For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass:

vulg: consideravit enim se et abiit et statim oblitus est qualis fuerit
clem: consideravit enim se, et abiit, et statim oblitus est qualis fuerit.
tr: κατενοησεν γαρ εαυτον και απεληλυθεν και ευθεως επελαθετο οποιος ην
kjv: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.

vulg: qui autem perspexerit in lege perfecta libertatis et permanserit non auditor obliviosus factus sed factor operis hic beatus in facto suo erit
clem: Qui autem perspexerit in legem perfectam libertatis, et permanserit in ea, non auditor obliviosus factus, sed factor operis: hic beatus in facto suo erit.
tr: ο δε παρακυψας εις νομον τελειον τον της ελευθεριας και παραμεινας ουτος ουκ ακροατης επιλησμονης γενομενος αλλα ποιητης εργου ουτος μακαριος εν τη ποιησει αυτου εσται
kjv: But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.

vulg: si quis autem putat se religiosum esse non refrenans linguam suam sed seducens cor suum huius vana est religio
clem: Si quis autem putat se religiosum esse, non refrenans linguam suam, sed seducens cor suum, hujus vana est religio.
tr: ει τις δοκει θρησκος ειναι εν υμιν μη χαλιναγωγων γλωσσαν αυτου αλλ απατων καρδιαν αυτου τουτου ματαιος η θρησκεια
kjv: If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man's religion is vain.

vulg: religio munda et inmaculata apud Deum et Patrem haec est visitare pupillos et viduas in tribulatione eorum inmaculatum se custodire ab hoc saeculo
clem: Religio munda et immaculata apud Deum et Patrem, hc est: visitare pupillos et viduas in tribulatione eorum, et immaculatum se custodire ab hoc sculo.
tr: θρησκεια καθαρα και αμιαντος παρα τω θεω και πατρι αυτη εστιν επισκεπτεσθαι ορφανους και χηρας εν τη θλιψει αυτων ασπιλον εαυτον τηρειν απο του κοσμου
kjv: Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.

vulg: fratres mei nolite in personarum acceptione habere fidem Domini nostri Iesu Christi gloriae
clem: Fratres mei, nolite in personarum acceptione habere fidem Domini nostri Jesu Christi glori.
tr: αδελφοι μου μη εν προσωποληψιαις εχετε την πιστιν του κυριου ημων ιησου χριστου της δοξης
kjv: My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.

vulg: etenim si introierit in conventu vestro vir aureum anulum habens in veste candida introierit autem et pauper in sordido habitu
clem: Etenim si introierit in conventum vestrum vir aureum annulum habens in veste candida, introierit autem et pauper in sordido habitu,
tr: εαν γαρ εισελθη εις την συναγωγην υμων ανηρ χρυσοδακτυλιος εν εσθητι λαμπρα εισελθη δε και πτωχος εν ρυπαρα εσθητι
kjv: For if there come unto your assembly a man with a gold ring, in goodly apparel, and there come in also a poor man in vile raiment;

vulg: et intendatis in eum qui indutus est veste praeclara et dixeritis tu sede hic bene pauperi autem dicatis tu sta illic aut sede sub scabillo pedum meorum
clem: et intendatis in eum qui indutus est veste prclara, et dixeritis ei: Tu sede hic bene: pauperi autem dicatis: Tu sta illic; aut sede sub scabello pedum meorum:
tr: και επιβλεψητε επι τον φορουντα την εσθητα την λαμπραν και ειπητε αυτω συ καθου ωδε καλως και τω πτωχω ειπητε συ στηθι εκει η καθου ωδε υπο το υποποδιον μου
kjv: And ye have respect to him that weareth the gay clothing, and say unto him, Sit thou here in a good place; and say to the poor, Stand thou there, or sit here under my footstool:

vulg: nonne iudicatis apud vosmet ipsos et facti estis iudices cogitationum iniquarum
clem: nonne judicatis apud vosmetipsos, et facti estis judices cogitationum iniquarum?
tr: και ου διεκριθητε εν εαυτοις και εγενεσθε κριται διαλογισμων πονηρων
kjv: Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?

vulg: audite fratres mei dilectissimi nonne Deus elegit pauperes in hoc mundo divites in fide et heredes regni quod repromisit Deus diligentibus se
clem: Audite, fratres mei dilectissimi: nonne Deus elegit pauperes in hoc mundo, divites in fide, et hredes regni, quod repromisit Deus diligentibus se?
tr: ακουσατε αδελφοι μου αγαπητοι ουχ ο θεος εξελεξατο τους πτωχους του κοσμου τουτου πλουσιους εν πιστει και κληρονομους της βασιλειας ης επηγγειλατο τοις αγαπωσιν αυτον
kjv: Hearken, my beloved brethren, Hath not God chosen the poor of this world rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he hath promised to them that love him?

vulg: vos autem exhonorastis pauperem nonne divites per potentiam opprimunt vos et ipsi trahunt vos ad iudicia
clem: vos autem exhonorastis pauperem. Nonne divites per potentiam opprimunt vos, et ipsi trahunt vos ad judicia?
tr: υμεις δε ητιμασατε τον πτωχον ουχ οι πλουσιοι καταδυναστευουσιν υμων και αυτοι ελκουσιν υμας εις κριτηρια
kjv: But ye have despised the poor. Do not rich men oppress you, and draw you before the judgment seats?

vulg: nonne ipsi blasphemant bonum nomen quod invocatum est super vos
clem: nonne ipsi blasphemant bonum nomen, quod invocatum est super vos?
tr: ουκ αυτοι βλασφημουσιν το καλον ονομα το επικληθεν εφ υμας
kjv: Do not they blaspheme that worthy name by the which ye are called?

vulg: si tamen legem perficitis regalem secundum scripturas diliges proximum tuum sicut te ipsum bene facitis
clem: Si tamen legem perficitis regalem secundum Scripturas: Diliges proximum tuum sicut teipsum: bene facitis:
tr: ει μεντοι νομον τελειτε βασιλικον κατα την γραφην αγαπησεις τον πλησιον σου ως σεαυτον καλως ποιειτε
kjv: If ye fulfil the royal law according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself, ye do well:

vulg: si autem personas accipitis peccatum operamini redarguti a lege quasi transgressores
clem: si autem personas accipitis, peccatum operamini, redarguti a lege quasi transgressores.
tr: ει δε προσωποληπτειτε αμαρτιαν εργαζεσθε ελεγχομενοι υπο του νομου ως παραβαται
kjv: But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.

vulg: quicumque autem totam legem servaverit offendat autem in uno factus est omnium reus
clem: Quicumque autem totam legem servaverit, offendat autem in uno, factus est omnium reus.
tr: οστις γαρ ολον τον νομον τηρησει πταισει δε εν ενι γεγονεν παντων ενοχος
kjv: For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all.

vulg: qui enim dixit non moechaberis dixit et non occides quod si non moechaberis occides autem factus es transgressor legis
clem: Qui enim dixit: Non mchaberis, dixit et: Non occides. Quod si non mchaberis, occides autem, factus es transgressor legis.
tr: ο γαρ ειπων μη μοιχευσης ειπεν και μη φονευσης ει δε ου μοιχευσεις φονευσεις δε γεγονας παραβατης νομου
kjv: For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if thou commit no adultery, yet if thou kill, thou art become a transgressor of the law.

vulg: sic loquimini et sic facite sicut per legem libertatis incipientes iudicari
clem: Sic loquimini, et sic facite sicut per legem libertatis incipientes judicari.
tr: ουτως λαλειτε και ουτως ποιειτε ως δια νομου ελευθεριας μελλοντες κρινεσθαι
kjv: So speak ye, and so do, as they that shall be judged by the law of liberty.

vulg: iudicium enim sine misericordia illi qui non fecit misericordiam superexultat autem misericordia iudicio
clem: Judicium enim sine misericordia illi qui non fecit misericordiam: superexaltat autem misericordia judicium.
tr: η γαρ κρισις ανιλεως τω μη ποιησαντι ελεος και κατακαυχαται ελεος κρισεως
kjv: For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.

vulg: quid proderit fratres mei si fidem quis dicat se habere opera autem non habeat numquid poterit fides salvare eum
clem: Quid proderit, fratres mei, si fidem quis dicat se habere, opera autem non habeat? numquid poterit fides salvare eum?
tr: τι το οφελος αδελφοι μου εαν πιστιν λεγη τις εχειν εργα δε μη εχη μη δυναται η πιστις σωσαι αυτον
kjv: What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?

vulg: si autem frater aut soror nudi sunt et indigent victu cotidiano
clem: Si autem frater et soror nudi sint, et indigeant victu quotidiano,
tr: εαν δε αδελφος η αδελφη γυμνοι υπαρχωσιν και λειπομενοι ωσιν της εφημερου τροφης
kjv: If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food,

vulg: dicat autem aliquis de vobis illis ite in pace calefacimini et saturamini non dederitis autem eis quae necessaria sunt corporis quid proderit
clem: dicat autem aliquis ex vobis illis: Ite in pace, calefacimini et saturamini: non dederitis autem eis qu necessaria sunt corpori, quid proderit?
tr: ειπη δε τις αυτοις εξ υμων υπαγετε εν ειρηνη θερμαινεσθε και χορταζεσθε μη δωτε δε αυτοις τα επιτηδεια του σωματος τι το οφελος
kjv: And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit?

vulg: sic et fides si non habeat opera mortua est in semet ipsam
clem: Sic et fides, si non habeat opera, mortua est in semetipsa.
tr: ουτως και η πιστις εαν μη εργα εχη νεκρα εστιν καθ εαυτην
kjv: Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.

vulg: sed dicet quis tu fidem habes et ego opera habeo ostende mihi fidem tuam sine operibus et ego ostendam tibi ex operibus fidem meam
clem: Sed dicet quis: Tu fidem habes, et ego opera habeo: ostende mihi fidem tuam sine operibus: et ego ostendam tibi ex operibus fidem meam.
tr: αλλ ερει τις συ πιστιν εχεις καγω εργα εχω δειξον μοι την πιστιν σου εκ  χωρις  των εργων σου καγω δειξω σοι εκ των εργων μου την πιστιν μου
kjv: Yea, a man may say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.

vulg: tu credis quoniam unus est Deus bene facis et daemones credunt et contremescunt
clem: Tu credis quoniam unus est Deus: bene facis: et dmones credunt, et contremiscunt.
tr: συ πιστευεις οτι ο θεος εις εστιν καλως ποιεις και τα δαιμονια πιστευουσιν και φρισσουσιν
kjv: Thou believest that there is one God; thou doest well: the devils also believe, and tremble.

vulg: vis autem scire o homo inanis quoniam fides sine operibus otiosa est
clem: Vis autem scire, o homo inanis, quoniam fides sine operibus mortua est?
tr: θελεις δε γνωναι ω ανθρωπε κενε οτι η πιστις χωρις των εργων νεκρα εστιν
kjv: But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?

vulg: Abraham pater noster nonne ex operibus iustificatus est offerens Isaac filium suum super altare
clem: Abraham pater noster nonne ex operibus justificatus est, offerens Isaac filium suum super altare?
tr: αβρααμ ο πατηρ ημων ουκ εξ εργων εδικαιωθη ανενεγκας ισαακ τον υιον αυτου επι το θυσιαστηριον
kjv: Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he had offered Isaac his son upon the altar?

vulg: vides quoniam fides cooperabatur operibus illius et ex operibus fides consummata est
clem: Vides quoniam fides cooperabatur operibus illius: et ex operibus fides consummata est?
tr: βλεπεις οτι η πιστις συνηργει τοις εργοις αυτου και εκ των εργων η πιστις ετελειωθη
kjv: Seest thou how faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect?

vulg: et suppleta est scriptura dicens credidit Abraham Deo et reputatum est illi ad iustitiam et amicus Dei appellatus est
clem: Et suppleta est Scriptura, dicens: Credidit Abraham Deo, et reputatum est illi ad justitiam, et amicus Dei appellatus est.
tr: και επληρωθη η γραφη η λεγουσα επιστευσεν δε αβρααμ τω θεω και ελογισθη αυτω εις δικαιοσυνην και φιλος θεου εκληθη
kjv: And the scripture was fulfilled which saith, Abraham believed God, and it was imputed unto him for righteousness: and he was called the Friend of God.

vulg: videtis quoniam ex operibus iustificatur homo et non ex fide tantum
clem: Videtis quoniam ex operibus justificatur homo, et non ex fide tantum?
tr: ορατε  τοινυν οτι εξ εργων δικαιουται ανθρωπος και ουκ εκ πιστεως μονον
kjv: Ye see then how that by works a man is justified, and not by faith only.

vulg: similiter autem et Raab meretrix nonne ex operibus iustificata est suscipiens nuntios et alia via eiciens
clem: Similiter et Rahab meretrix, nonne ex operibus justificata est, suscipiens nuntios, et alia via ejiciens?
tr: ομοιως δε και ρααβ η πορνη ουκ εξ εργων εδικαιωθη υποδεξαμενη τους αγγελους και ετερα οδω εκβαλουσα
kjv: Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?

vulg: sicut enim corpus sine spiritu emortuum est ita et fides sine operibus mortua est
clem: Sicut enim corpus sine spiritu mortuum est, ita et fides sine operibus mortua est.
tr: ωσπερ γαρ το σωμα χωρις πνευματος νεκρον εστιν ουτως και η πιστις χωρις των εργων νεκρα εστιν
kjv: For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

vulg: nolite plures magistri fieri fratres mei scientes quoniam maius iudicium sumitis
clem: Nolite plures magistri fieri fratres mei, scientes quoniam majus judicium sumitis.
tr: μη πολλοι διδασκαλοι γινεσθε αδελφοι μου ειδοτες οτι μειζον κριμα ληψομεθα
kjv: My brethren, be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation.

vulg: in multis enim offendimus omnes si quis in verbo non offendit hic perfectus est vir potens etiam freno circumducere totum corpus
clem: In multis enim offendimus omnes. Si quis in verbo non offendit, hic perfectus est vir: potest etiam freno circumducere totum corpus.
tr: πολλα γαρ πταιομεν απαντες ει τις εν λογω ου πταιει ουτος τελειος ανηρ δυνατος χαλιναγωγησαι και ολον το σωμα
kjv: For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man, and able also to bridle the whole body.

vulg: si autem equorum frenos in ora mittimus ad consentiendum nobis et omne corpus illorum circumferimus
clem: Si autem equis frena in ora mittimus ad consentiendum nobis, et omne corpus illorum circumferimus.
tr: ιδου των ιππων τους χαλινους εις τα στοματα βαλλομεν προς το πειθεσθαι αυτους ημιν και ολον το σωμα αυτων μεταγομεν
kjv: Behold, we put bits in the horses' mouths, that they may obey us; and we turn about their whole body.

vulg: ecce et naves cum magnae sint et a ventis validis minentur circumferuntur a modico gubernaculo ubi impetus dirigentis voluerit
clem: Ecce et naves, cum magn sint, et a ventis validis minentur, circumferuntur a modico gubernaculo ubi impetus dirigentis voluerit.
tr: ιδου και τα πλοια τηλικαυτα οντα και υπο σκληρων ανεμων ελαυνομενα μεταγεται υπο ελαχιστου πηδαλιου οπου αν η ορμη του ευθυνοντος βουληται
kjv: Behold also the ships, which though they be so great, and are driven of fierce winds, yet are they turned about with a very small helm, whithersoever the governor listeth.

vulg: ita et lingua modicum quidem membrum est et magna exultat ecce quantus ignis quam magnam silvam incendit
clem: Ita et lingua modicum quidem membrum est, et magna exaltat. Ecce quantus ignis quam magnam silvam incendit!
tr: ουτως και η γλωσσα μικρον μελος εστιν και μεγαλαυχει ιδου ολιγον πυρ ηλικην υλην αναπτει
kjv: Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!

vulg: et lingua ignis est universitas iniquitatis lingua constituitur in membris nostris quae maculat totum corpus et inflammat rotam nativitatis nostrae inflammata a gehenna
clem: Et lingua ignis est, universitas iniquitatis. Lingua constituitur in membris nostris, qu maculat totum corpus, et inflammat rotam nativitatis nostr inflammata a gehenna.
tr: και η γλωσσα πυρ ο κοσμος της αδικιας ουτως η γλωσσα καθισταται εν τοις μελεσιν ημων η σπιλουσα ολον το σωμα και φλογιζουσα τον τροχον της γενεσεως και φλογιζομενη υπο της γεεννης
kjv: And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell.

vulg: omnis enim natura bestiarum et volucrum et serpentium etiam ceterorum domantur et domita sunt a natura humana
clem: Omnis enim natura bestiarum, et volucrum, et serpentium, et ceterorum domantur, et domita sunt a natura humana:
tr: πασα γαρ φυσις θηριων τε και πετεινων ερπετων τε και εναλιων δαμαζεται και δεδαμασται τη φυσει τη ανθρωπινη
kjv: For every kind of beasts, and of birds, and of serpents, and of things in the sea, is tamed, and hath been tamed of mankind:

vulg: linguam autem nullus hominum domare potest inquietum malum plena veneno mortifero
clem: linguam autem nullus hominum domare potest: inquietum malum, plena veneno mortifero.
tr: την δε γλωσσαν ουδεις δυναται ανθρωπων δαμασαι ακατασχετον κακον μεστη ιου θανατηφορου
kjv: But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.

vulg: in ipsa benedicimus Dominum et Patrem et in ipsa maledicimus homines qui ad similitudinem Dei facti sunt
clem: In ipsa benedicimus Deum et Patrem: et in ipsa maledicimus homines, qui ad similitudinem Dei facti sunt.
tr: εν αυτη ευλογουμεν τον θεον και πατερα και εν αυτη καταρωμεθα τους ανθρωπους τους καθ ομοιωσιν θεου γεγονοτας
kjv: Therewith bless we God, even the Father; and therewith curse we men, which are made after the similitude of God.

vulg: ex ipso ore procedit benedictio et maledictio non oportet fratres mei haec ita fieri
clem: Ex ipso ore procedit benedictio et maledictio. Non oportet, fratres mei, hc ita fieri.
tr: εκ του αυτου στοματος εξερχεται ευλογια και καταρα ου χρη αδελφοι μου ταυτα ουτως γινεσθαι
kjv: Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.

vulg: numquid fons de eodem foramine emanat dulcem et amaram aquam
clem: Numquid fons de eodem foramine emanat dulcem et amaram aquam?
tr: μητι η πηγη εκ της αυτης οπης βρυει το γλυκυ και το πικρον
kjv: Doth a fountain send forth at the same place sweet water and bitter?

vulg: numquid potest fratres mei ficus olivas facere aut vitis ficus sic neque salsa dulcem potest facere aquam
clem: Numquid potest, fratres mei, ficus uvas facere, aut vitis ficus? Sic neque salsa dulcem potest facere aquam.
tr: μη δυναται αδελφοι μου συκη ελαιας ποιησαι η αμπελος συκα ουτως ουδεμια πηγη αλυκον και γλυκυ ποιησαι υδωρ
kjv: Can the fig tree, my brethren, bear olive berries? either a vine, figs? so can no fountain both yield salt water and fresh.

vulg: quis sapiens et disciplinatus inter vos ostendat ex bona conversatione operationem suam in mansuetudine sapientiae
clem: Quis sapiens et disciplinatus inter vos? Ostendat ex bona conversatione operationem suam in mansuetudine sapienti.
tr: τις σοφος και επιστημων εν υμιν δειξατω εκ της καλης αναστροφης τα εργα αυτου εν πραυτητι σοφιας
kjv: Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge among you? let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom.

vulg: quod si zelum amarum habetis et contentiones in cordibus vestris nolite gloriari et mendaces esse adversus veritatem
clem: Quod si zelum amarum habetis, et contentiones sint in cordibus vestris: nolite gloriari, et mendaces esse adversus veritatem:
tr: ει δε ζηλον πικρον εχετε και εριθειαν εν τη καρδια υμων μη κατακαυχασθε και ψευδεσθε κατα της αληθειας
kjv: But if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not, and lie not against the truth.

vulg: non est ista sapientia desursum descendens sed terrena animalis diabolica
clem: non est enim ista sapientia desursum descendens: sed terrena, animalis, diabolica.
tr: ουκ εστιν αυτη η σοφια ανωθεν κατερχομενη αλλ επιγειος ψυχικη δαιμονιωδης
kjv: This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.

vulg: ubi enim zelus et contentio ibi inconstantia et omne opus pravum
clem: Ubi enim zelus et contentio, ibi inconstantia et omne opus pravum.
tr: οπου γαρ ζηλος και εριθεια εκει ακαταστασια και παν φαυλον πραγμα
kjv: For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.

vulg: quae autem desursum est sapientia primum quidem pudica est deinde pacifica modesta suadibilis plena misericordia et fructibus bonis non iudicans sine simulatione
clem: Qu autem desursum est sapientia, primum quidem pudica est, deinde pacifica, modesta, suadibilis, bonus consentiens, plena misericordia et fructibus bonis, non judicans, sine simulatione.
tr: η δε ανωθεν σοφια πρωτον μεν αγνη εστιν επειτα ειρηνικη επιεικης ευπειθης μεστη ελεους και καρπων αγαθων αδιακριτος και ανυποκριτος
kjv: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be intreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.

vulg: fructus autem iustitiae in pace seminatur facientibus pacem
clem: Fructus autem justiti, in pace seminatur, facientibus pacem.
tr: καρπος δε της δικαιοσυνης εν ειρηνη σπειρεται τοις ποιουσιν ειρηνην
kjv: And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace of them that make peace.

vulg: unde bella et lites in vobis nonne hinc ex concupiscentiis vestris quae militant in membris vestris
clem: Unde bella et lites in vobis? nonne hinc: ex concupiscentiis vestris, qu militant in membris vestris?
tr: ποθεν πολεμοι και μαχαι εν υμιν ουκ εντευθεν εκ των ηδονων υμων των στρατευομενων εν τοις μελεσιν υμων
kjv: From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members?

vulg: concupiscitis et non habetis occiditis et zelatis et non potestis adipisci litigatis et belligeratis non habetis propter quod non postulatis
clem: concupiscitis, et non habetis: occiditis, et zelatis: et non potestis adipisci: litigatis, et belligeratis, et non habetis, propter quod non postulatis.
tr: επιθυμειτε και ουκ εχετε φονευετε και ζηλουτε και ου δυνασθε επιτυχειν μαχεσθε και πολεμειτε ουκ εχετε δε δια το μη αιτεισθαι υμας
kjv: Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain: ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not.

vulg: petitis et non accipitis eo quod male petatis ut in concupiscentiis vestris insumatis
clem: Petitis, et non accipitis: eo quod male petatis: ut in concupiscentiis vestris insumatis.
tr: αιτειτε και ου λαμβανετε διοτι κακως αιτεισθε ινα εν ταις ηδοναις υμων δαπανησητε
kjv: Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.

vulg: adulteri nescitis quia amicitia huius mundi inimica est Dei quicumque ergo voluerit amicus esse saeculi huius inimicus Dei constituitur
clem: Adulteri, nescitis quia amicitia hujus mundi inimica est Dei? quicumque ergo voluerit amicus esse sculi hujus, inimicus Dei constituitur.
tr: μοιχοι και μοιχαλιδες ουκ οιδατε οτι η φιλια του κοσμου εχθρα του θεου εστιν ος αν ουν βουληθη φιλος ειναι του κοσμου εχθρος του θεου καθισταται
kjv: Ye adulterers and adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God.

vulg: aut putatis quia inaniter scriptura dicat ad invidiam concupiscit Spiritus qui inhabitat in nobis
clem: An putatis quia inaniter Scriptura dicat: Ad invidiam concupiscit spiritus qui habitat in vobis?
tr: η δοκειτε οτι κενως η γραφη λεγει προς φθονον επιποθει το  πνευμα  ο κατωκησεν εν ημιν
kjv: Do ye think that the scripture saith in vain, The spirit that dwelleth in us lusteth to envy?

vulg: maiorem autem dat gratiam propter quod dicit Deus superbis resistit humilibus autem dat gratiam
clem: majorem autem dat gratiam. Propter quod dicit: Deus superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam.
tr: μειζονα δε διδωσιν χαριν διο λεγει ο θεος υπερηφανοις αντιτασσεται ταπεινοις δε διδωσιν χαριν
kjv: But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.

vulg: subditi igitur estote Deo resistite autem diabolo et fugiet a vobis
clem: Subditi ergo estote Deo, resistite autem diabolo, et fugiet a vobis.
tr: υποταγητε ουν τω θεω αντιστητε τω διαβολω και φευξεται αφ υμων
kjv: Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

vulg: adpropiate Domino et adpropinquabit vobis emundate manus peccatores et purificate corda duplices animo
clem: Appropinquate Deo, et appropinquabit vobis. Emundate manus, peccatores: et purificate corda, duplices animo.
tr: εγγισατε τω θεω και εγγιει υμιν καθαρισατε χειρας αμαρτωλοι και αγνισατε καρδιας διψυχοι
kjv: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.

vulg: miseri estote et lugete et plorate risus vester in luctum convertatur et gaudium in maerorem
clem: Miseri estote, et lugete, et plorate: risus vester in luctum convertatur, et gaudium in mrorem.
tr: ταλαιπωρησατε και πενθησατε και κλαυσατε ο γελως υμων εις πενθος μεταστραφητω και η χαρα εις κατηφειαν
kjv: Be afflicted, and mourn, and weep: let your laughter be turned to mourning, and your joy to heaviness.

vulg: humiliamini in conspectu Domini et exaltabit vos
clem: Humiliamini in conspectu Domini, et exaltabit vos.
tr: ταπεινωθητε ενωπιον του κυριου και υψωσει υμας
kjv: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up.

vulg: nolite detrahere de alterutrum fratres qui detrahit fratri aut qui iudicat fratrem suum detrahit legi et iudicat legem si autem iudicas legem non es factor legis sed iudex
clem: Nolite detrahere alterutrum fratres. Qui detrahit fratri, aut qui judicat fratrem suum, detrahit legi, et judicat legem. Si autem judicas legem, non es factor legis, sed judex.
tr: μη καταλαλειτε αλληλων αδελφοι ο καταλαλων αδελφου και κρινων τον αδελφον αυτου καταλαλει νομου και κρινει νομον ει δε νομον κρινεις ουκ ει ποιητης νομου αλλα κριτης
kjv: Speak not evil one of another, brethren. He that speaketh evil of his brother, and judgeth his brother, speaketh evil of the law, and judgeth the law: but if thou judge the law, thou art not a doer of the law, but a judge.

vulg: unus est legislator et iudex qui potest perdere et liberare tu autem quis es qui iudicas proximum
clem: Unus est legislator et judex, qui potest perdere et liberare.
tr: εις εστιν ο νομοθετης ο δυναμενος σωσαι και απολεσαι συ τις ει ος κρινεις τον ετερον
kjv: There is one lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy: who art thou that judgest another?

vulg: ecce nunc qui dicitis hodie aut crastino ibimus in illam civitatem et faciemus quidem ibi annum et mercabimur et lucrum faciemus
clem: Tu autem quis es, qui judicas proximum? Ecce nunc qui dicitis: Hodie, aut crastino ibimus in illam civitatem, et faciemus ibi quidem annum, et mercabimur, et lucrum faciemus:
tr: αγε νυν οι λεγοντες σημερον και  η  αυριον πορευσωμεθα  πορευσομεθα  εις τηνδε την πολιν και ποιησωμεν ποιησομεν εκει ενιαυτον ενα και εμπορευσωμεθα και κερδησωμεν εμπορευσομεθα και κερδησομεν
kjv: Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain:

vulg: qui ignoratis quid erit in crastinum quae enim est vita vestra vapor est ad modicum parens deinceps exterminatur
clem: qui ignoratis quid erit in crastino.
tr: οιτινες ουκ επιστασθε το της αυριον ποια γαρ η ζωη υμων ατμις γαρ εστιν η προς ολιγον φαινομενη επειτα δε αφανιζομενη
kjv: Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.

vulg: pro eo ut dicatis si Dominus voluerit et vixerimus faciemus hoc aut illud
clem: Qu est enim vita vestra? vapor est ad modicum parens, et deinceps exterminabitur; pro eo ut dicatis: Si Dominus voluerit. Et: Si vixerimus, faciemus hoc, aut illud.
tr: αντι του λεγειν υμας εαν ο κυριος θεληση και ζησωμεν και ποιησωμεν  ζησομεν και ποιησομεν  τουτο η εκεινο
kjv: For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.

vulg: nunc autem exultatis in superbiis vestris omnis exultatio talis maligna est
clem: Nunc autem exsultatis in superbiis vestris. Omnis exsultatio talis, maligna est.
tr: νυν δε καυχασθε εν ταις αλαζονειαις υμων πασα καυχησις τοιαυτη πονηρα εστιν
kjv: But now ye rejoice in your boastings: all such rejoicing is evil.

vulg: scienti igitur bonum facere et non facienti peccatum est illi
clem: Scienti igitur bonum facere, et non facienti, peccatum est illi.
tr: ειδοτι ουν καλον ποιειν και μη ποιουντι αμαρτια αυτω εστιν
kjv: Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.

vulg: age nunc divites plorate ululantes in miseriis quae advenient vobis
clem: Agite nunc divites, plorate ululantes in miseriis vestris, qu advenient vobis.
tr: αγε νυν οι πλουσιοι κλαυσατε ολολυζοντες επι ταις ταλαιπωριαις υμων ταις επερχομεναις
kjv: Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you.

vulg: divitiae vestrae putrefactae sunt et vestimenta vestra a tineis comesta sunt
clem: Diviti vestr putrefact sunt, et vestimenta vestra a tineis comesta sunt.
tr: ο πλουτος υμων σεσηπεν και τα ιματια υμων σητοβρωτα γεγονεν
kjv: Your riches are corrupted, and your garments are motheaten.

vulg: aurum et argentum vestrum eruginavit et erugo eorum in testimonium vobis erit et manducabit carnes vestras sicut ignis thesaurizastis in novissimis diebus
clem: Aurum et argentum vestrum ruginavit: et rugo eorum in testimonium vobis erit, et manducabit carnes vestras sicut ignis. Thesaurizastis vobis iram in novissimis diebus.
tr: ο χρυσος υμων και ο αργυρος κατιωται και ο ιος αυτων εις μαρτυριον υμιν εσται και φαγεται τας σαρκας υμων ως πυρ εθησαυρισατε εν εσχαταις ημεραις
kjv: Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days.

vulg: ecce merces operariorum qui messuerunt regiones vestras qui fraudatus est a vobis clamat et clamor ipsorum in aures Domini Sabaoth introiit
clem: Ecce merces operariorum, qui messuerunt regiones vestras, qu fraudata est a vobis, clamat: et clamor eorum in aures Domini sabbaoth introivit.
tr: ιδου ο μισθος των εργατων των αμησαντων τας χωρας υμων ο απεστερημενος αφ υμων κραζει και αι βοαι των θερισαντων εις τα ωτα κυριου σαβαωθ εισεληλυθασιν
kjv: Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of the Lord of sabaoth.

vulg: epulati estis super terram et in luxuriis enutristis corda vestra in die occisionis
clem: Epulati estis super terram, et in luxuriis enutristis corda vestra in die occisionis.
tr: ετρυφησατε επι της γης και εσπαταλησατε εθρεψατε τας καρδιας υμων ως εν ημερα σφαγης
kjv: Ye have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton; ye have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter.

vulg: addixistis occidistis iustum non resistit vobis
clem: Addixistis, et occidistis justum, et non resistit vobis.
tr: κατεδικασατε εφονευσατε τον δικαιον ουκ αντιτασσεται υμιν
kjv: Ye have condemned and killed the just; and he doth not resist you.

vulg: patientes igitur estote fratres usque ad adventum Domini ecce agricola expectat pretiosum fructum terrae patienter ferens donec accipiat temporivum et serotinum
clem: Patientes igitur estote, fratres, usque ad adventum Domini. Ecce agricola exspectat pretiosum fructum terr, patienter ferens donec accipiat temporaneum et serotinum.
tr: μακροθυμησατε ουν αδελφοι εως της παρουσιας του κυριου ιδου ο γεωργος εκδεχεται τον τιμιον καρπον της γης μακροθυμων επ αυτω εως αν λαβη υετον πρωιμον και οψιμον
kjv: Be patient therefore, brethren, unto the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, and hath long patience for it, until he receive the early and latter rain.

vulg: patientes estote et vos confirmate corda vestra quoniam adventus Domini adpropinquavit
clem: Patientes igitur estote et vos, et confirmate corda vestra: quoniam adventus Domini appropinquavit.
tr: μακροθυμησατε και υμεις στηριξατε τας καρδιας υμων οτι η παρουσια του κυριου ηγγικεν
kjv: Be ye also patient; stablish your hearts: for the coming of the Lord draweth nigh.

vulg: nolite ingemescere fratres in alterutrum ut non iudicemini ecce iudex ante ianuam adsistit
clem: Nolite ingemiscere, fratres, in alterutrum, ut non judicemini. Ecce judex ante januam assistit.
tr: μη στεναζετε κατ αλληλων αδελφοι ινα μη κατακριθητε ιδου  ο  κριτης προ των θυρων εστηκεν
kjv: Grudge not one against another, brethren, lest ye be condemned: behold, the judge standeth before the door.

vulg: exemplum accipite fratres laboris et patientiae prophetas qui locuti sunt in nomine Domini
clem: Exemplum accipite, fratres, exitus mali, laboris, et patienti, prophetas qui locuti sunt in nomine Domini.
tr: υποδειγμα λαβετε της κακοπαθειας αδελφοι μου και της μακροθυμιας τους προφητας οι ελαλησαν τω ονοματι κυριου
kjv: Take, my brethren, the prophets, who have spoken in the name of the Lord, for an example of suffering affliction, and of patience.

vulg: ecce beatificamus qui sustinuerunt sufferentiam Iob audistis et finem Domini vidistis quoniam misericors est Dominus et miserator
clem: Ecce beatificamus eos qui sustinuerunt. Sufferentiam Job audistis, et finem Domini vidistis, quoniam misericors Dominus est, et miserator.
tr: ιδου μακαριζομεν τους υπομενοντας την υπομονην ιωβ ηκουσατε και το τελος κυριου ειδετε οτι πολυσπλαγχνος εστιν ο κυριος και οικτιρμων
kjv: Behold, we count them happy which endure. Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord; that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy.

vulg: ante omnia autem fratres mei nolite iurare neque per caelum neque per terram neque aliud quodcumque iuramentum sit autem vestrum est est non non uti non sub iudicio decidatis
clem: Ante omnia autem, fratres mei, nolite jurare, neque per clum, neque per terram, neque aliud quodcumque juramentum. Sit autem sermo vester: Est, est: Non, non: ut non sub judicio decidatis.
tr: προ παντων δε αδελφοι μου μη ομνυετε μητε τον ουρανον μητε την γην μητε αλλον τινα ορκον ητω δε υμων το ναι ναι και το ου ου ινα μη εις υποκρισιν  υπο κρισιν  πεσητε
kjv: But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.

vulg: tristatur aliquis vestrum oret aequo animo est psallat
clem: Tristatur aliquis vestrum? oret. quo animo est? psallat.
tr: κακοπαθει τις εν υμιν προσευχεσθω ευθυμει τις ψαλλετω
kjv: Is any among you afflicted? let him pray. Is any merry? let him sing psalms.

vulg: infirmatur quis in vobis inducat presbyteros ecclesiae et orent super eum unguentes eum oleo in nomine Domini
clem: Infirmatur quis in vobis? inducat presbyteros ecclesi, et orent super eum, ungentes eum oleo in nomine Domini:
tr: ασθενει τις εν υμιν προσκαλεσασθω τους πρεσβυτερους της εκκλησιας και προσευξασθωσαν επ αυτον αλειψαντες αυτον ελαιω εν τω ονοματι του κυριου
kjv: Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord:

vulg: et oratio fidei salvabit infirmum et adlevabit eum Dominus et si in peccatis sit dimittentur ei
clem: et oratio fidei salvabit infirmum, et alleviabit eum Dominus: et si in peccatis sit, remittentur ei.
tr: και η ευχη της πιστεως σωσει τον καμνοντα και εγερει αυτον ο κυριος καν αμαρτιας η πεποιηκως αφεθησεται αυτω
kjv: And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him.

vulg: confitemini ergo alterutrum peccata vestra et orate pro invicem ut salvemini multum enim valet deprecatio iusti adsidua
clem: Confitemini ergo alterutrum peccata vestra, et orate pro invicem ut salvemini: multum enim valet deprecatio justi assidua.
tr: εξομολογεισθε αλληλοις τα παραπτωματα και ευχεσθε υπερ αλληλων οπως ιαθητε πολυ ισχυει δεησις δικαιου ενεργουμενη
kjv: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.

vulg: Helias homo erat similis nobis passibilis et oratione oravit ut non plueret super terram et non pluit annos tres et menses sex
clem: Elias homo erat similis nobis passibilis: et oratione oravit ut non pluret super terram, et non pluit annos tres, et menses sex.
tr: ηλιας ανθρωπος ην ομοιοπαθης ημιν και προσευχη προσηυξατο του μη βρεξαι και ουκ εβρεξεν επι της γης ενιαυτους τρεις και μηνας εξ
kjv: Elias was a man subject to like passions as we are, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain: and it rained not on the earth by the space of three years and six months.

vulg: et rursum oravit et caelum dedit pluviam et terra dedit fructum suum
clem: Et rursum oravit: et clum dedit pluviam, et terra dedit fructum suum.
tr: και παλιν προσηυξατο και ο ουρανος υετον εδωκεν και η γη εβλαστησεν τον καρπον αυτης
kjv: And he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth her fruit.

vulg: fratres mei si quis ex vobis erraverit a veritate et converterit quis eum
clem: Fratres mei, si quis ex vobis erraverit a veritate, et converterit quis eum:
tr: αδελφοι εαν τις εν υμιν πλανηθη απο της αληθειας και επιστρεψη τις αυτον
kjv: Brethren, if any of you do err from the truth, and one convert him;

vulg: scire debet quoniam qui converti fecerit peccatorem ab errore viae suae salvabit animam eius a morte et operit multitudinem peccatorum
clem: scire debet quoniam qui converti fecerit peccatorem ab errore vi su, salvabit animam ejus a morte, et operiet multitudinem peccatorum.
tr: γινωσκετω οτι ο επιστρεψας αμαρτωλον εκ πλανης οδου αυτου σωσει ψυχην εκ θανατου και καλυψει πληθος αμαρτιων
kjv: Let him know, that he which converteth the sinner from the error of his way shall save a soul from death, and shall hide a multitude of sins.
